question_text: The period of a simple pendulum depends on:
explanation: T = 2π√(L/g), independent of mass and amplitude for small oscillations

question_text: A pendulum of length 1 m has a period of 2 seconds. What is the period if the length is increased to 4 m?
A body of mass 5 kg is acted upon by two perpendicular forces of 8 N and 6 N. What is the magnitude of the acceleration?
explanation: Resultant force = √(8²+6²) = 10 N; a = F/m = 10/5 = 2 m/s²

question_text: A ball is thrown at an angle of 30° to the horizontal with a velocity of 20 m/s. What is the maximum height reached? (g = 10 m/s²)
The range of a projectile fired at 60° with velocity 20 m/s is (g = 10 m/s²):
Three forces of magnitudes 3 N, 4 N, and 5 N act at a point. Which of the following could NOT be the magnitude of their resultant?
explanation: Maximum resultant = 12 N (all in same direction). Minimum resultant = 0 N (can form a triangle with 3,4,5). Values between 0 and 12 inclusive are possible. 13 N exceeds the maximum, so it is impossible.

question_text: A uniform rod of weight 50 N and length 2 m is supported horizontally by two parallel strings at its ends. A weight of 30 N is hung 0.5 m from one end. Calculate the tension in the string nearer to the load.
explanation: Taking moments about the far end: T_near × 2 = (50 × 1) + (30 × 1.5) = 50 + 45 = 95 ⇒ T_near = 47.5 N

question_text: A couple consists of two forces of magnitude 20 N each, acting parallel but opposite in direction, separated by a distance of 0.5 m. Calculate the moment of the couple.
explanation: Moment of couple = Force × perpendicular distance = 20 × 0.5 = 10 Nm

question_text: A body is in equilibrium under the action of three forces. Which of the following is true?
explanation: For three forces in equilibrium, they must be concurrent (meet at a point) or parallel.

question_text: A weight of 100 N is suspended by two strings making angles of 30° and 60° with the vertical. Calculate the tension in the string making 30° with the vertical.
explanation: T₁sin30° = T₂sin60°; T₁cos30° + T₂cos60° = 100; Solving: T₁ = 86.6 N

question_text: A ladder of length 5 m and weight 200 N rests against a smooth vertical wall with its base on rough ground 3 m from the wall. What is the frictional force at the base?
explanation: Let angle θ, cosθ = 3/5, sinθ = 4/5; Taking moments about base: R_wall×4 = 200×1.5; R_wall = 75 N; Friction = R_wall = 75 N

question_text: A block and tackle system has 5 pulleys. If the efficiency is 80%, what effort is needed to lift a load of 400 N?
explanation: VR = 5; MA = Efficiency×VR/100% = 80×5/100 = 4; Effort = Load/MA = 400/4 = 100 N

question_text: The work done in moving a body of mass 5 kg through a height of 2 m against gravity is (g = 10 m/s²):
explanation: Work = mgh = 5×10×2 = 100 J

question_text: A 2 kg object falls freely from a height of 20 m. What is its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: KE at ground = Initial PE = mgh = 2×10×20 = 400 J

question_text: A bullet of mass 0.02 kg is fired with a velocity of 200 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A force of 50 N is used to push a box horizontally through a distance of 10 m. If the force is applied at an angle of 30° to the horizontal, what is the work done?
A 1000 W electric motor lifts a load of 500 N to a height of 20 m. How long does it take?
explanation: Power = Work/time = Force×distance/time; 1000 = 500×20/t; t = 10000/1000 = 10 s

question_text: A body of mass 4 kg has a momentum of 20 kgm/s. What is its kinetic energy?
explanation: p = mv, so v = p/m = 20/4 = 5 m/s; KE = ½mv² = ½×4×25 = 50 J

question_text: The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called:
explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.

question_text: A stone of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 15 m/s. What is its potential energy at the highest point? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: At highest point, KE converted to PE; Initial KE = ½×0.5×225 = 56.25 J; PE at top = 56.25 J

question_text: A boy of mass 40 kg runs up a flight of 20 stairs each of height 15 cm in 10 seconds. Calculate his power. (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Total height = 20×0.15 = 3 m; Work = mgh = 40×10×3 = 1200 J; Power = 1200/10 = 120 W

question_text: A vehicle of mass 1000 kg is moving with a velocity of 20 m/s. What is the braking force required to stop it in 50 m?
explanation: Work done by brake = Change in KE; F×50 = ½×1000×400; F = 200,000/50 = 4000 N

question_text: A body of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 10 m. What is its velocity just before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
A pump raises 1000 kg of water through a height of 20 m in 5 minutes. What is the power of the pump? (g = 10 m/s²)
A machine lifts a load of 500 N through a distance of 2 m when an effort of 100 N moves through 12 m. What is the efficiency?
A block of mass 8 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface by a force of 40 N. If the coefficient of friction is 0.3, what is the acceleration? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Friction = μmg = 0.3×8×10 = 24 N; Net force = 40-24 = 16 N; a = 16/8 = 2 m/s²

question_text: The coefficient of friction between two surfaces is 0.4. What force is needed to just move a body of mass 10 kg placed on a horizontal surface? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Force needed = limiting friction = μmg = 0.4×10×10 = 40 N

question_text: A body of mass 5 kg is placed on a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. If the coefficient of friction is 0.2, will it slide down? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Component down plane = mgsin30° = 5×10×0.5 = 25 N; Friction up plane = μmgcos30° = 0.2×5×10×0.866 = 8.66 N; Net force = 16.34 N; a = 16.34/5 = 3.27 m/s²

question_text: The maximum static frictional force between two surfaces is 50 N. What force is needed to keep the body moving with constant velocity if the kinetic friction is 40 N?
explanation: To maintain constant velocity, applied force must equal kinetic friction = 40 N

question_text: Which of the following statements about friction is NOT true?
option_d: Friction depends on the nature of surfaces
explanation: Friction is not always undesirable; it helps in walking, braking, etc.

question_text: A body of mass 2 kg rests on a rough horizontal plane. A force of 8 N just moves it. What is the coefficient of static friction? (g = 10 m/s²)
A spring of length 20 cm is stretched to 25 cm by a force of 10 N. What is the spring constant?
explanation: Extension = 5 cm = 0.05 m; k = F/e = 10/0.05 = 200 N/m

question_text: A spring extends by 3 cm when a force of 6 N is applied. What force will cause an extension of 5 cm?
explanation: F ∝ e; F₂/F₁ = e₂/e₁; F₂/6 = 5/3; F₂ = 6×5/3 = 10 N

question_text: A rubber band of length 10 cm is stretched to 12 cm by a force of 2 N. What is the strain?
explanation: Strain = extension/original length = 2/10 = 0.2

question_text: A wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 10⁻⁶ m² is stretched by a force of 100 N. If Young's modulus is 2×10¹¹ N/m², what is the extension?
The stress on a wire is 2×10⁷ N/m² and the strain is 10⁻⁴. What is Young's modulus?
explanation: Y = stress/strain = 2×10⁷/10⁻⁴ = 2×10¹¹ N/m²

question_text: A force of 50 N is applied to a piston of area 0.02 m² in a hydraulic press. What pressure is transmitted through the fluid?
explanation: Pressure = Force/Area = 50/0.02 = 2500 Pa

question_text: A hydraulic lift has a small piston of area 0.01 m² and a large piston of area 0.5 m². What force must be applied to the small piston to lift a car of weight 10,000 N?
At what depth in water is the pressure equal to 3 atmospheres? (1 atm = 1.01×10⁵ Pa, ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Pressure due to water = 2 atm = 2.02×10⁵ Pa; h = P/ρg = 2.02×10⁵/(1000×10) = 20.2 m

question_text: A mercury barometer reads 76 cm. What is the atmospheric pressure in Pa? (ρ_mercury = 13600 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
The pressure at a point in a liquid is 20,000 Pa. What is the depth if the density of the liquid is 800 kg/m³? (g = 10 m/s²)
A U-tube contains water and oil. The water level is 15 cm higher on one side. If the density of oil is 800 kg/m³, what is the height of the oil column?
explanation: h_oil × ρ_oil = h_water × ρ_water; h_oil × 800 = 0.15 × 1000; h_oil = 150/800 = 0.1875 m = 18.75 cm

question_text: A gas is at a pressure of 2×10⁵ Pa in a cylinder of volume 0.1 m³. If the gas is compressed to 0.04 m³ at constant temperature, what is the new pressure?
A force of 100 N is applied to a small piston of area 0.005 m² in a hydraulic press. What is the force on the large piston of area 0.1 m²?
The pressure at a point in a liquid at rest depends on:
explanation: Pressure = hρg, depends on depth and density.

question_text: A 5 kg block is pulled with a force of 30 N at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. If the coefficient of friction is 0.3, what is the acceleration? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Horizontal force = 30cos30° = 30 × 0.866 = 25.98 N; Vertical upward force = 30sin30° = 15 N; Weight = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N; Normal reaction R = 50 – 15 = 35 N; Friction force = μR = 0.3 × 35 = 10.5 N; Net horizontal force = 25.98 – 10.5 = 15.48 N; Acceleration a = F_net / m = 15.48 / 5 = 3.096 m/s² ≈ 3.10 m/s²

question_text: How much heat is required to convert 2 kg of ice at 0°C to water at 0°C? (Latent heat of fusion of ice = 336,000 J/kg)
